newsitem.title: CANADA: Renaissance dives after reduced forecast.
newsitem.headline: Renaissance dives after reduced forecast.

text.p: Shares in Renaissance Energy Ltd were pounded by investors on Thursday after the company said its oil production in 1997 would be lower than previously forecast.
Calgary-based Renaissance was off 2.90 to 36.40 in busy early trade of 575,523 shares.
The senior producer said crude oil production was now expected to average 85,000 barrels a day this year, down from an earlier projection of 92,500.
Crude oil production averaged 71,920 barrels a day last year.
Renaissance said the reduced expectations were because of lower than expected second-quarter volumes due to bad weather which delayed drilling.

The company also recently completed an oil property review which indicated that second-half volume additions would be delayed while routine pressure maintenance programs were implemented and became effective in some oil pools in central, southern and Wapella operating regions.

In addition, Renaissance delayed scheduled development drilling of a new oil discovery in the Webb area of southwest Saskatchewan pending government review of an environmental assessment report, it said.
Natural gas volume expectations remained unchanged at 450 million cubic feet per day, Renaissance said.

The company's exploration and development drilling program was still underway, it said. Renaissance expected to drill about 1,000 more wells in 1997, bringing the total for the year to 1,800. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
